body.purpose: Chat prose, markdown, settings copy. Rides the user-set root font size (12-18px).

mono.purpose: Machine truth: commands, diffs, paths, daemon metadata, the sidebar roster (0.75rem/1.4 there).

title.purpose: Modal titles, sidebar section titles, row titles. Hierarchy by weight and color, not size.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked section headers, queue kinds, group headers, usage statuses.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Modals, lightbox image, mobile sidebar sheet. The only structural shadow.

shadows.name: card-kiss
shadows.purpose: Exactly one resting card (the pet). A quirk, not a precedent.

shadows.name: glow-success
shadows.purpose: Streaming/ready status dots. Glow is a lamp, not elevation.

shadows.name: asleep-ring
shadows.purpose: Asleep daemon dot: fakes a border while staying 8px round.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: The single transition duration; pairs with ease-out for bg/border/color state changes.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Defined but currently unused; reserve for larger surface transitions.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Easing for looping status animations (pulses, pet-bob).

motion.name: fresh-in
motion.purpose: Newly streamed markdown blocks fading in.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: sidebar becomes overlay sheet; sheets go full-viewport; settings nav rail swaps to tabs (tabs show at min-width 721px inverse).

components.name: Primary Button (Send)
components.description: The one primary action per view — send/spawn. Signal Blue fill, console-black text, weight 600.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent); border: 1px solid var(--accent); color: var(--bg); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.857rem; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 140ms ease-out, border-color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent), var(--bg) 12%); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent), var(--bg) 12%); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }

components.name: Base Button
components.description: Default control: quiet Control Surface fill that wakes to Hover Wash on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-base { background: var(--btn); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); color: var(--text); font-size: 0.857rem; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 140ms ease-out, border-color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-base:hover { background: var(--hover); } .ds-btn-base:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-base:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Roster/row actions: transparent and muted until hovered; arms red for destructive confirm.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 140ms ease-out, border-color 140ms ease-out, color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: var(--text); border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-ghost.ds-armed, .ds-btn-ghost.ds-armed:hover { color: var(--error); border-color: var(--error-border); }

components.name: Danger Button (Stop)
components.description: Destructive/interrupt actions in the Alarm Red trio.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: var(--stop-bg); border: 1px solid var(--error-border); color: var(--error-text); font-size: 0.857rem; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 140ms ease-out, border-color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--stop-bg), var(--error) 15%); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Sunken Console Well field; focus is the global 2px Signal Blue ring (search-style fields swap border instead).
components.css: .ds-input { background: var(--bg-deep); border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--text); font-size: 0.857rem; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Queue Chip
components.description: Queued prompts and filter chips: pill, hairline, semantic trio when carrying status.
components.html: queued rerun the failing suite 2 steering
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; background: var(--panel); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); color: var(--text); font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 1px 8px 1px 12px; border-radius: 999px; } .ds-chip-kind { text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted); } .ds-chip-warn { background: var(--warning-bg); border-color: var(--warning-border); color: var(--warning); padding: 1px 12px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; }

components.name: Daemon Status Dot
components.description: The roster ladder in one atom: idle, ready (glow), transitional (pulse), reconnecting, error, asleep (inset ring).
components.css: .ds-dot { display: inline-block; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted-2); margin-right: 8px; } .ds-dot.ds-ready { background: var(--success); box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--success); } .ds-dot.ds-busy { background: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--accent); animation: ds-dot-pulse 1.2s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-dot.ds-reconnecting { background: var(--warning); box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--warning); } .ds-dot.ds-error { background: var(--error); box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--error); } .ds-dot.ds-asleep { background: var(--muted-2); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-strong); } @keyframes ds-dot-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.4; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-dot.ds-busy { animation: none; } }

components.name: Tool Card
components.description: Every tool render's shell: flat panel, hairline, 8px radius, mono-capable body.
components.css: .ds-tool-card { background: var(--panel); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.857rem; color: var(--text); max-width: 420px; } .ds-tool-header { padding: 8px 12px; color: var(--muted-2); font-weight: 600; } .ds-tool-body { padding: 0 12px 8px; font-family: var(--font-mono); }

components.name: User Message Bubble
components.description: The only bubble in the system: the operator's own message, right-aligned in Signal Wash, max 80% width. Assistant messages are edge-to-edge.
components.html: respawn d3 on the design branch
components.css: .ds-msg-user { align-self: flex-end; background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--text); border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 12px; max-width: 80%; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; }

narrative.overview:
One operator, many agents. This UI is the flight-ops room for a fleet of disposable agent daemons: calm, watchful, exact. The screen's job is supervision, not conversation — surfaces recede so that status (dots, pills, chips, streamed text) can carry the signal. Nothing competes with the readouts.

Density follows the terminal, not the chat app: compact 2-24px spacing rhythm, machine truth set in monospace, labels in small tracked caps, controls that sit quiet until hovered. Depth is nearly absent by doctrine — structure comes from 1px hairlines and tonal panel steps, and shadow appears only when something floats above the console or when a status light glows.

The palette is a dark instrument panel first: near-black blue-gray surfaces, a softened white readout, and a single Signal Blue accent used with deliberate rarity. Five alternate palettes rebalance the same semantic slots.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first instrument panel; five alternate themes overriding only color tokens
Flat-by-default surfaces; 1px borders do the structural work
One accent, used rarely; status speaks in a semantic trio (bg + border + text)
Zero font assets — system sans + system mono only
Single 140ms ease-out motion vocabulary; six small keyframes; full prefers-reduced-motion teardown

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The accent appears on ≤10% of any screen — focus rings, the active selection, one primary action. If everything signals, nothing does.

rules.name: The Semantic Trio Rule
rules.body: A status is never a bare color. Every status surface ships background + border + text from the same trio; bare hue-on-neutral status fills are a defect.

rules.name: The Zero-Asset Rule
rules.body: No webfonts, ever. If a glyph can't come from the system stack, the design is wrong, not the stack.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Sans is the operator speaking; mono is the machine reporting. Never set machine output (commands, paths, logs, git state) in sans, and never set prose in mono.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow appears only on overlays (--shadow-2) or as a status glow. Adding a resting-state shadow to a card is a defect.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from 1px borders and tonal steps, never from shadow or whitespace alone. If a boundary matters, it gets a hairline.

dos: Do build every surface from the semantic tokens (var(--bg), var(--panel), …) so all six themes stay coherent; themes override colors only.
Do express status as the full trio (bg + border + text) — queued, ready, error, and diff states all follow it.
Do keep motion at 140ms ease-out (the single transition vocabulary) and gate anything animated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
Do set machine truth in the mono stack at 0.857rem or smaller; the roster lives at 0.75rem/1.4.
Do let assistant output run edge-to-edge; reserve bubbles for the operator's own messages.
Do reach for the pill + hairline + trio pattern for any new chip, badge, or status.
donts: Don't add resting-state shadows or elevation to cards, buttons, or the sidebar (The Flat-By-Default Rule).
Don't introduce gradients, glassmorphism, backdrop-blur chrome, or glow on non-status elements.
Don't chat-app the surface: no avatar pairs, no messenger bubble symmetry, no emoji-forward empty states.
Don't load a webfont or hard-code a font family outside the two system stacks (The Zero-Asset Rule).
Don't invent one-off colors, radii, or spacing outside the token scales; extend the scale or reuse a rung.
Don't use the breakdown data-viz ramp for status, or status hues in charts — the ramps are deliberately disjoint.
